# The Shipit file

A `Shipit` file describes how a project is built and served. It is real
[Starlark](https://starlark-lang.org/): `shipit generate` (or the default
`auto` mode) writes one for you by detecting the project type, and from that
point on the file is yours — edit it, extend it, or replace it entirely.

```python
# Generated by Shipit v0.21.7 — https://github.com/wasmerio/shipit
# This file is yours to edit: add steps or override the serve below.

load("//shipit/tools:python.shipit", "python_build", "python_serve")

build = python_build(config)

python_serve(config, build, name = "my-app")
```

Every provider ships as a pair of functions in the bundled standard library:

- `<provider>_build(config, ...)` returns a **build struct**: the build
  steps, the packages the runtime will need because of this build, the
  mounts it filled, and env vars the serve must set.
- `<provider>_serve(config, build, ...)` wires a serve around any build
  struct: start command, runtime deps, env, mounts, services.

The seam between the two is the composition point. A static-site generator
pairs its own build with the shared static serve; Laravel is a PHP build
with a Node asset build folded into its phases; mkdocs is a Python build
feeding a static serve. Your file can do the same.

For projects living in a subdirectory of the workspace, the generated file
carries a marker the CLI reads back:

```python
app_subdir = "apps/dashboard"
```

## Customizing a generated file

Every `<provider>_serve` accepts the same override surface (forwarded to the
generic assembler in `//shipit:serve.shipit`):

| Parameter        | Effect                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`           | Deployment name (generated files bake the directory name) |
| `provider`       | Deployment identity label (defaults per provider)       |
| `build_pre`      | Steps to run before the build struct's steps            |
| `build_post`     | Steps to run after the build struct's steps             |
| `extra_deps`     | Additional runtime packages                             |
| `extra_env`      | Additional serve-time env vars                          |
| `extra_commands` | Additional command entries                              |
| `commands`       | Base commands dict (`start`, `after_deploy`, ...)       |
| `env`            | Serve-time env vars (merged with the build's)           |
| `prepare`        | Commands run once after the build, before serving       |
| `cwd`            | Working directory of the serve                          |
| `mounts` / `volumes` / `services` | Extra mounts, persistent volumes, services |

```python
load("//shipit/tools:node.shipit", "node_build", "node_serve")

build = node_build(config)

node_serve(
    config,
    build,
    name = "my-app",
    build_post = [run("node scripts/prerender.js", group = "build")],
    extra_env = {"NODE_ENV": "production"},
    services = [service("db", "postgres")],
)
```

Conditional steps are idiomatic: `None` entries in step lists are dropped,
so `run("...") if config.app_subdir else None` works anywhere steps go.

## Builtins

These are available in every Shipit file and stdlib module:

| Builtin                                    | Meaning                                        |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `dep(name, version = None)`                 | A package (build or runtime dependency)        |
| `use(*deps)`                                | Make packages available to later build steps   |
| `run(cmd, group=, inputs=, outputs=)`       | Run a shell command during the build           |
| `copy(source, target = None, ignore=, base=)` | Copy from the project (or `base = "assets"`) |
| `workdir(path)`                             | Change the build working directory             |
| `env(**vars)`                               | Set env vars for subsequent build steps        |
| `write(path, content)`                      | Write a file during the build                  |
| `path(dir)`                                 | Prepend a directory to `PATH`                  |
| `mount(name)`                               | A named mount: `.path` (build) / `.serve_path` (serve) |
| `volume(name, serve_path)`                  | A persistent volume mounted at serve time      |
| `service(name, provider)`                   | A backing service: `postgres`, `mysql`, `redis` |
| `file_exists(relpath)`                      | Probe the app source tree (see below)          |
| `config`                                    | The detected provider config (entry file only) |
| `PORT`                                      | The configured port, as a string               |

`run()` groups (`install`, `build`, `prune`, ...) tag steps so CLI command
overrides know which step to replace. `$PORT` inside `start`/`after_deploy`
commands is substituted with the configured port.

### `file_exists()`

`file_exists("package.json")` checks the app source tree — the workspace
root, or the app subdirectory for subdir projects. Paths are app-relative;
absolute paths and `..` traversal are rejected. Symlinks are followed, so a
symlinked `wp-content/` counts. Use it for plain existence checks; derived
or overridable values belong in `config`.

## Configuration

The `config` global is the provider's detected configuration. Every field
can be overridden without touching the file:

- **Environment variables** with the `SHIPIT_` prefix:
  `SHIPIT_PHPIX=true`, `SHIPIT_NODE_VERSION=22`, `SHIPIT_WP_VERSION=latest`,
  `SHIPIT_PYTHON_VERSION=3.12`, `SHIPIT_STATIC_DIR=dist`, ...
- **`--config` JSON** merged over the detected values:
  `shipit build --config '{"phpix": true, "php_version": "8.4"}'`
- **CLI command flags**: `--install-command`, `--build-command`, and
  `--start-command` replace the first step of the matching group (or the
  start command) in the evaluated plan.

Notable fields per provider (see `src/shipit/providers/*.py` for the full
sets — common fields `name`, `port`, and `app_subdir` live on the base):

| Provider   | Fields                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| python     | `python_version`, `server`, `framework`, `extra_dependencies`, `precompile_python`, `database` |
| node       | `node_version`, `package_manager`, `build_command`, `optimize_node_dependencies` |
| php        | `php_version`, `phpix`, `use_composer`, `composer_build_script`, `public_dir` |
| wordpress  | php fields plus `wp_version`, `wp_locale`, `wp_cli_version`    |
| staticfile | `static_dir`, `sws_version`, `convert_redirects`               |
| go         | `go_version`, `go_build_file`, `serve_binary`                  |

## `load()` labels

| Label form                     | Resolves to                                   |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `//shipit/...:file.shipit`     | The bundled standard library                  |
| `//pkg/path:file.shipit`       | `<project root>/pkg/path/file.shipit`         |
| `file.shipit` / `./file.shipit`| Relative to the loading file                  |

So a project can keep its own helpers in `deploy/custom.shipit` and load
them with `load("//deploy:custom.shipit", "my_helper")`.

## Provider reference

| Provider    | Module                              | Build / Serve                          |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| python      | `//shipit/tools:python.shipit`      | `python_build` / `python_serve`        |
| node        | `//shipit/tools:node.shipit`        | `node_build` / `node_serve`            |
| go          | `//shipit/tools:go.shipit`          | `go_build` / `go_serve`                |
| php         | `//shipit/tools:php.shipit`         | `php_build` / `php_serve`              |
| laravel     | `//shipit/tools:laravel.shipit`     | `laravel_build` / `laravel_serve`      |
| wordpress   | `//shipit/tools:wordpress.shipit`   | `wordpress_build` / `wordpress_serve`  |
| staticfile  | `//shipit/tools:staticfile.shipit`  | `staticfile_build` / `staticfile_serve` |
| hugo        | `//shipit/tools:hugo.shipit`        | `hugo_build` / `staticfile_serve`      |
| jekyll      | `//shipit/tools:jekyll.shipit`      | `jekyll_build` / `staticfile_serve`    |
| mkdocs      | `//shipit/tools:mkdocs.shipit`      | `mkdocs_build` / `staticfile_serve`    |
| node-static | `//shipit/tools:node_static.shipit` | `nodestatic_build` / `staticfile_serve` |

The static family shares one serve: their generated files pass the identity
explicitly — `staticfile_serve(config, build, provider = "hugo")` — because
the `provider` label is deployment identity and belongs to the serve, not
the build.

Providers with flavors take keyword options on the build. The most useful:
`python_build(config, serving = False)` and Node's granular fragments
(`node_toolchain`, `node_install_steps`, `node_build_step`, ...) give you
embeddable builds for composing.

## Composing your own

The stdlib composes the same way user files do. This is a docs site built
by a Python tool and served as static files — essentially what
`mkdocs.shipit` does internally:

```python
load("//shipit:serve.shipit", "build")
load("//shipit/tools:python.shipit", "python_build")
load("//shipit/tools:staticfile.shipit", "staticfile_serve")

py = python_build(config, serving = False)
site = mount("static_app")

docs = build(
    steps = py.steps + [
        run("uv run mkdocs build --site-dir={}".format(site.path), group = "build"),
    ],
    serve_deps = py.serve_deps,
    mounts = [site],
    static_app = site,
    static_config = None,
)

staticfile_serve(config, docs, name = "docs", provider = "mkdocs")
```

`build()` (from `//shipit:serve.shipit`) creates a build struct from steps
plus the convention fields (`serve_deps`, `mounts`, `env`) and any extra
fields downstream serves want — here the `static_app` mount that
`staticfile_serve` reads. `serve()` from the same module is the generic
assembler behind every `<provider>_serve`, with the override surface
documented above.
